intervention.title: Keep derived values out of source-only fields
intervention.summary: Change the collection and publication path so source observations, authorized calculations, and missing values remain distinguishable in future outputs.

purpose.p: Prevent inferred values presented as observations by preserving a field's meaning through collection and serialization. An accurate calculation can still violate a source-only contract.

precondition.p: The task or output format distinguishes source-reported fields from calculations, and that distinction is being lost or bypassed.
The maintainer can change the collector instructions, serializer, or publication template and its consumers without silently changing the agreed output contract.

step.p: Update the reusable collector and serializer to keep an observed value tied to its source location. Permit calculations only in explicitly authorized derived fields, with their formula and inputs; preserve the contract's missing-value representation.

Remove formula fallbacks and guessed defaults from source-only assignments. When the source lacks a value, publish the agreed missing marker rather than a computed substitute. If the current format cannot express the distinction, leave that field missing and report the limitation.

Check the final publication path with one observed value, a genuine zero, a missing value, and an authorized calculation. Confirm that serialization and display retain each meaning; use the existing data model where it can express these distinctions.
Review subsequent comparable outputs against available source evidence, including outputs that look complete and those with missing fields.

evaluation.p: Predict fewer unsupported non-missing values in source-only fields, with genuine observations and permitted calculations preserved. Compare published values with accessible sources and inspect whether downstream consumers retain the distinction.

More missing values may reflect honest uncertainty, lost access, or a broken collector. Check useful data coverage and publication success alongside provenance accuracy. Correct source records with misleading rendered labels point to the publication layer; this change will not repair unrelated date filters or arithmetic errors.

risks-and-confounders.p: Overstrict handling can discard valid observations, convert real zeros to missing values, or break consumers expecting a complete row. Source changes and inaccessible source pages limit retrospective assessment.

stop-and-rollback.p: Repair or revert the faulty collector or serializer if valid data is lost or publication breaks. Preserve the observed-versus-derived distinction in a compatible output or an explicit limitation; do not reinstate silent fabrication as the fallback.
